U: For a full layer system, the largest index i with |L_i| != 1, or zero if every layer is a singleton. During warmup U=0. Indices start at 1.

full_cache_miss: If j=0, reset B=tau and use prediction eviction from the entire cache; this eviction does not consume B.
Otherwise, find the smallest i>=j with |cache intersect (L_1 union ... union L_i)|=i. These cached pages are the legal eviction candidates.

On that support miss, evaluate the gate; if true increment B and the gate-credit count by one. If B>0, decrement B by one and use prediction eviction from the candidates; otherwise use priority eviction.
Prediction eviction chooses the candidate with greatest stored prediction score, breaking ties by greatest page ID. Priority eviction chooses the candidate of lowest persistent random rank.
algorithm_rules.initial_state: Empty cache, k empty ordered layers L_1..L_k, Y=0, credit budget B=0. Each miss costs one, including warmup. Forgiveness is disabled.
layer_updates: If L_1 is empty and j=0: drop L_1, shift remaining layers left, append {p}.
Otherwise if j=0 and k=1: replace the layers with [{p}]. If j=0 and k>1: replace the last two layers with their union, then append {p}; earlier layers stay in order.
If j=1: drop L_1, shift remaining layers left, append {p}.
If j>=2: replace adjacent layers L_(j-1), L_j with (L_(j-1) union L_j) minus {p}, keeping all other layers in order, then append {p}.
algorithm_rules.priority_updates: After updating layers, remove pages that left support. Insert p at a uniformly random rank if it is newly in support. Other pages keep their relative ranks; hits do not rerandomize existing priorities. Use the stated seed.
algorithm_rules.serve_request: On a miss insert p after any eviction. With free cache space, insert without eviction or gate evaluation. On every request store the supplied prediction for p, then update layers, then assign Y according to the profile. Layer updates happen on hits too. Y is assigned, never incremented.
algorithm_rules.support: Support is the union of the layers. Requested page p is in layer j, or j=0 if outside support. A support miss means p is in support but absent from the cache. U and Y in the gate are their values BEFORE the current request's layer update.
algorithm_rules.task: Choose a paired experiment and precommit both predictions. The tool first checks mathematical feasibility, then executes an accepted plan. A rejection is not an experiment result. You have at most two planning turns. After a rejected plan or a non-discriminating measurement, use the feedback to choose an untried case. Return only the four fields in planning_output_schema as JSON, with a concise hypothesis of 10 to 1000 characters. The backend invokes the reviewed adapter after validating your plan. A discriminating result ends experimentation and requires a scoped finding. Do not claim that a control rules out effects on other inputs.

gate: On a support miss, earn one credit if U <= (Y+2)/e - 2; spend a positive credit on prediction eviction.

history_profiles.after_miss: Assign Y := U AFTER serving a miss and updating layers. Hits leave Y unchanged.
history_profiles.after_request: Assign Y := U AFTER every request and its layer update, including hits.

input_scope: constructed development diagnostics, not published experimental replications
question: Which available experiment best distinguishes whether gate-history timing affects behavior?
